title: Moroccan Chicken Pastilla
summary: Spiced shredded chicken, honeyed onions, soft eggs and cinnamon-sugar almonds in a crisp buttered filo case, finished with icing sugar and a cinnamon lattice.
equipment: large deep frying pan or wide pot with lid
25 cm ovenproof frying pan or deep pie dish

ingredients.item: fresh coriander, leaves and tender stems, finely chopped
fine sea salt or table salt
sheets filo (phyllo) pastry, about 30 x 40 cm

steps.title: Soften the onions
steps.text: Heat the oil in the large pan over medium-low heat. Add the onions, cover and cook for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until very soft and translucent. Stir in the coriander, garlic, ginger, turmeric, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, saffron if using, salt and pepper and cook for 3 minutes until fragrant. Cooking the onions slowly under a lid draws out their sweetness, which becomes the base of the whole filling.

steps.title: Simmer the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken and the water, bring to a simmer, then cover and cook gently for 30-35 minutes until tender. The thickest piece should read at least 74 °C, though thighs are most tender at about 80 °C. Lift the chicken out, leave it to cool a little, and shred it into bite-size pieces.

steps.title: Make it jammy
steps.text: Stir the honey into the onions and cook uncovered over medium-low heat for 20-25 minutes, stirring often, until golden and jammy with no liquid left. Leave to cool. Cooking off all the liquid is the key to a crisp base, because the filo can only stay flaky over a dry filling.

steps.title: Toast the almonds
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan). Toast the almonds on the tray for 8-10 minutes until golden, then cool and chop or crush them coarsely. Mix with the caster sugar and 1 tsp cinnamon. Toasting brings out a deeper, nuttier flavour that balances the sweetness.

steps.title: Scramble the eggs
steps.text: Beat the eggs and set 1 tbsp aside for glazing. Melt the 10 g butter in the small pan over medium-low heat and scramble the eggs gently for 3-4 minutes, until fully set with no runny egg left (71 °C). Cool. Soft, small curds give the filling a tender layer without making it wet.

steps.title: Line the pan
steps.text: Keep the oven at 180 °C (160 °C fan) and brush the 25 cm pan with melted butter. Brush 6 filo sheets with butter, one at a time, and lay them overlapping in a pinwheel so they cover the base and hang well over the rim. Spread the chicken over the base, then the onions, the eggs and finally the almond mixture, pressing each layer level.

steps.title: Close the pie
steps.text: Fold the overhanging filo up over the filling. Brush the remaining 4 sheets with butter and lay them on top, tucking their edges down the sides to make a neat, sealed round. Mix the last of the butter with the reserved egg and brush it over the top, which helps it bake to an even, shiny gold.

steps.title: Bake until crisp
steps.text: Bake for 40-45 minutes, until the top is deep golden and crisp all over; the centre should read at least 74 °C. Because the fillings are already cooked, this bake is mainly about crisping the pastry and heating everything through.

steps.title: Dust and serve
steps.text: Leave the pie in the pan for 10 minutes, then slide it onto a board. Sift the icing sugar evenly over the top, then sift or drizzle the cinnamon in crossing lines to form a lattice. Cut into 8 wedges and serve warm.

tips: Make sure every filling is cool before assembling; warm fillings steam the filo and make it tear.
The most common mistake is leaving the onions wet. Keep cooking until the pan is almost dry, or the base will turn soggy.
The chicken, onions and eggs can be cooked up to 2 days ahead and chilled, so the pie only needs assembling and baking on the day.
Dust with the icing sugar and cinnamon just before serving so the topping stays crisp and does not dissolve on the warm pastry.
storage: Keep leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat at 180 °C (160 °C fan) for about 20 minutes, until crisp and piping hot (74 °C), then dust with a little more icing sugar and cinnamon. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
